_comment: Stage A/B relation screening thresholds. These encode a policy rather than
an invariant, which is why they live here and not in the code: a reader may
reasonably want to inspect them or vary them without editing screening
logic. The effective values are written into
past run's thresholds stay recoverable from its own output.
Frozen hyperparameters, expected row counts and the forbidden column set are
deliberately NOT here. Those are invariants the code asserts against, and
the friction of changing them is the point.
Every key below is required. A missing or unknown key is rejected rather
than defaulted, so a typo cannot silently loosen a threshold.

structural._comment: A relation failing any of these is structurally rejected.

_comment: Stricter than the structural gates, for the `preferred` decision. The
cap on preferred relations bounds how many variants the next stage trains.
Expressed as PR-AUC lift over the base rate, so they do not depend on the
fraud prevalence of the partition being screened.
require_signal_above_missingness is the gate that caught card_core_addr1:
a relation's history summaries must beat its own key-missingness
indicator, or the apparent signal is the missingness sentinel.
